results.description:
In May of 193 AD, Emperor Pertinax was murdered by the Praetorian Guard, triggering a chaotic auction for the imperial throne. This episode explores the brief but violent reign of Didius Julianus, who literally bought the empire from the soldiers who killed his predecessor. We examine how this desperate transaction exposed the fragility of Roman succession and sparked civil wars across three provinces: Britain, Syria, and the Danube. Join us as we trace the rise of Septimius Severus, the brutal suppression of the Pescennius Niger rebellion, and the political maneuvering that reshaped the legions forever. This is a deep dive into the moment Rome nearly tore itself apart over gold.

results.description:
The disappearance of the Ninth Hispana legion has puzzled historians for centuries. While many assume they were wiped out in Britain, evidence suggests a different fate. This episode explores the archaeological record, the inscription at York, and the possibility that the legion was relocated to the Near East before its eventual dissolution. We examine the role of Hadrian’s Wall, the strategic shifts in Roman military deployment, and why some legions vanish from the historical record while others endure. Join Lucas and Luna as they piece together fragments of stone and text to reveal the true story behind one of Rome’s most famous military mysteries.

results.collectionName: The Roman Empire: How Rome Ruled the Ancient World — Fexingo History
results.description:
In this episode, we explore the secret world of Roman glass production, a technology that transformed daily life across the Mediterranean. Lucas and Luna trace the evolution from expensive, hand-blown luxury items to mass-produced everyday ware. We dive into the workshops of Syria and Judea, where artisans perfected core-forming techniques before the invention of the blowpipe revolutionized the industry. The conversation examines how cobalt and manganese became the colors of imperial taste, turning humble sand into vibrant blue and purple vessels found as far north as Vindolanda. We also look at the archaeological evidence preserved in Pompeii, revealing the dangerous heat and precise chemistry required to create these fragile masterpieces. This is a story of industrial innovation, global trade, and the quiet magic of alchemy that made light and color accessible to ordinary Romans.

results.description:
We often think of the Roman Empire as a machine built on legions and laws, but its foundation was cracked by the people it sought to own. In this episode, we trace the violent arc of the Third Servile War, focusing not just on Spartacus the gladiator, but on the broader ecosystem of slave revolts that haunted Rome from Sicily to Gaul. We explore how Ennodius Pamphilus, a former slave who became a powerful senator in Mediolanum, navigated the treacherous path from chains to consulship. Through the lens of inscriptions and fragmented accounts, we examine the brutal efficiency of Marcus Licinius Crassus’s campaign against the rebels and the political maneuvering that followed. This story reveals how slavery wasn't just an economic backdrop but a constant, simmering threat that forced Rome to constantly renegotiate its own identity and power.
